objects.evidenceText: The slide states that IEEE standards drive functionality, capability and interoperability of products and services affecting how people live, work and communicate.
objects.reason: The complete sentence is legible in both the embedded object and the original slide. It is a general presentation statement, not a numerical membership fact.

objects.evidenceText: The slide illustrates six standards-process stage labels arranged around a colored ring: initiating the project, mobilizing the working group, drafting the standard, balloting the standard, gaining final approval, and maintaining the standard.
objects.reason: The ring image alone contains no text; the stage labels are separate visible native text on the same original slide. The ring has no numeric proportions, so it must not support percentage claims.

objects.evidenceText: The slide's IEEE 802.11 membership chart shows a historical series from about 1991 through 2025, with a rise to the mid-2000s, a decline around 2008, and a renewed rise after 2020 to the highest plotted level at the right edge.
objects.reason: The axis and broad trajectory are legible on the crop and original slide. Exact yearly point values are not labeled and must not be inferred from this rendering.

objects.evidenceText: The slide's MAC randomization timeline says: 2014 iOS 8 adds randomization during scanning/probe requests; 2015 Android 6.0 introduces it for background scans; 2016 Windows 10 introduces conditional support when hardware supports it; 2018 Android 9 adds randomization when connecting as a developer option; 2019 Android 10 adds randomization when connecting, enabled by default; 2020 iOS 14 adds randomization when connecting, enabled by default.
objects.reason: All six date/label pairs are legible on the original image. This records the presentation's dated timeline, not a current platform support claim.

objects.evidenceText: The frequency/wavelength schematic marks mmWave between 30 and 300 GHz, corresponding approximately to 1 cm down to 1 mm wavelength; it places microwave below, and THz, far infrared, infrared and UV toward higher frequency/shorter wavelength.
objects.reason: The mmWave boundaries and scale labels are visible. The diagram is schematic; do not read exact band allocations or device performance from it.
